goal: Prevents bitcoind from crashing via std::terminate when a buffered write fails, instead allowing normal error handling
Protects node operators running on storage that can fill up, such as during block or undo writes
reviewability: Ready to review: small, self-contained fix with a reproducer and regression test
CI is clean and mergeable, no unresolved material requests
agreement: Concept ACK with no objections raised (w0xlt)
Author's explanation of terminate-vs-normal-error-path answered a reviewer's question without pushback (andrewtoth)
A broader systemic-fix wish was raised but not framed as an objection to this PR (maflcko)

categories.name: indexes
why: P3 because it only changes the failure mode on block/undo write errors, not the outcome
The node still has to stop either way, so the benefit is a clean shutdown instead of an abrupt terminate
Narrow edge case limited to disk-full-mid-write scenarios rather than data correctness

categories.name: utils
why: P2 because the fix touches a shared serialization primitive used broadly across the node
Fixes a subtle noexcept-destructor-throws bug that could otherwise cause node-wide crashes
Same latent pattern could recur at other BufferedWriter call sites, raising the value of fixing it here
